lignesRisque.risques: - crushing of workers by the various site machinery/loads
lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
-Draw up the site layout plan in consultation with the client (MO) and the safety coordinator (CSS, if appointed)
- a person in charge is designated to organise deliveries, site traffic and the guiding of machinery
- installation of adequate signage (see signage section)
'- Definition and marking-out of the different traffic zones

lignesRisque.sourceDanger: Uncontrolled access of vehicles and pedestrians
lignesRisque.risques: -Accidents involving people from outside the site
lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Fence off work zones located alongside roads and put up signs: "No entry to the site".
- Wear and require the wearing of high-visibility work clothing (hi-vis vest as a minimum)
- Sign-post and mark out the access routes
- Stabilisation and maintenance of the track

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.risques: - objects falling within the site area
lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention: -Enforce the ban on moving outside the work zones and pedestrian traffic zones, and enforce the wearing of a hard hat

- Determine the secure parking zones both on the plan and on site
- Wear high-visibility work clothing
- Switch on the vehicle's beacon light when working at night
- If the location is hidden, either wait until daylight or direct traffic and mark the site.

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once
Possible if multiple issues occur simultaneously

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Installation of traffic warning signs. 
-Work alongside roads is prohibited without marking-out. 
-Compliance with the highway code and the instructions of the competent authorities.

- use of steel plates under the outriggers of the crane truck
- assessment and stabilisation of the area in case of doubt
- use of inspected equipment only

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention: - use of inspected slings

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once
Possible if multiple issues occur simultaneously

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention: - guiding the load by means of a rope

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- marking-out of the zone.
- Prohibition on moving underneath the load.

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.risques: - damage to existing cables or pipes
lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- prior consultation with the project supervisor or their representative in case of works near existing cables or pipes
- exploratory trial pit

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention: - Dampen the area in strong wind.

- Marking-out of the work zone with barrier tape and stakes at 1.5 m from the edge
- Installation of a fall-prevention barrier
- Covering of the zone as work progresses
- Installation of footbridges with integrated guardrails on paths crossing the trench

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Connection carried out by a competent electrician. 
- Acceptance inspection of the installation before commissioning
- Preparatory work carried out with the power off before connection
- Lock-out/tag-out (consignation)
-Entrance door and locker room cabinets fitted with a locking system

lignesRisque.risques: - contamination due to lack of hygiene
lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Ban on eating meals in the changing room
- Ensure each company's role in tidying and cleaning is clear
- Ensure proper tidying and cleaning at each shift change (at least once a day)
- Ensure sorting and disposal of waste in the appropriate containers

probabilite.texte: Possible if multiple issues occur simultaneously
Possible if multiple issues occur simultaneously

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Comply with and enforce the ban on placing clothing on heaters
- Ensure sufficient fire extinguishers are present nearby
- Comply with and enforce the smoking ban.
- Visual inspection before switching off and leaving the premises at the end of each shift or day.

lignesRisque.risques: - contamination due to lack of hygiene (facilities shared with subcontractor/other company)
lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Ensure each company's role in tidying and cleaning is clear
- Ensure proper tidying and cleaning at each shift change (at least once a day)
- Ensure sorting and disposal of waste in the appropriate containers

lignesRisque.risques: - lack of warmth in winter, hypothermia
lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention: - installation of heaters

probabilite.texte: Possible if multiple issues occur simultaneously

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Comply with and enforce the ban on placing clothing on heaters
- Ensure sufficient fire extinguishers are present nearby
- Comply with and enforce the smoking ban.
- Visual inspection before switching off and leaving the premises at the end of each shift or day.

- Ensure each company's role in tidying and cleaning is clear
- Ensure proper tidying and cleaning at each shift change (at least once a day)
- Ensure sorting and disposal of waste in the appropriate containers
- visual inspection by the team leader and/or a designated person in charge
- Comply with and enforce basic hygiene rules (posters, toolbox talks, etc.)

-Provide sufficient lighting (no shadow areas, etc.) in dangerous or dark zones
-Preferably use white light (the light must not affect the colours of the safety signage)
-Shield reflective surfaces so that the lighting does not dazzle people

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.risques: Fall / fall into an excavation / sprain
lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Keep traffic routes in good condition: remove large stones, fill in holes, etc.
- Keep access routes clear
- Mark out excavations
- Regularly tidy the site
- Stay alert while moving around

lignesRisque.sourceDanger: Absent or reduced visibility of people moving around the site
lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Wear and enforce the wearing of the hi-vis vest to increase visibility
- Keep the beacon light on (for site machinery) at all times while moving
- Do not wear MP3 players or similar; keep the radio volume low while driving.
- Stay alert while moving around
- Be accompanied by a banksman/guide when necessary and when the track is congested or visibility is reduced

lignesRisque.sourceDanger: Uncontrolled traffic from outside the site
lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- No moving around the site with private vehicles.
- No parking of private vehicles on the site (except in specially designated areas).

- Do not exceed the vehicle's maximum authorised load
- Fit a warning panel when items project more than one metre behind the vehicle
- Properly secure items placed on the vehicle's roof rack using straps

lignesRisque.sourceDanger:
- lack of attention
-internal/external visibility
-non-compliance with the rules
when driving a vehicle or machine
lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- No mobile phone use while driving.
- Stay alert to pedestrians and other machinery.
- Comply with the traffic plan where one exists.
- Operational reversing alarm on trucks, forklifts, etc.
- Orange beacon light always active
- Wear high-visibility work clothing
- If necessary, designate a banksman to guide drivers during manoeuvres and handling operations.
- Check the condition of the vehicle before setting off (headlights, tyres, brakes, oil level, clean windows, fire extinguisher, first-aid kit…)

probabilite.texte: Possible if multiple issues occur simultaneously

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- A designated person organises deliveries, site traffic and the guiding of machinery
- Unloading only in the zones shown on the site layout plan, or with the agreement of the client (MO) and/or safety coordinator (CSS) for any other zones. 
- Installation of steel plates under the crane's outriggers if the ground bearing capacity is insufficient. 
- Manoeuvre carried out by a competent operator
- Use of slings that are in good condition and inspected (visual and quarterly inspection)

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.sourceDanger: - Defective equipment leading to an accident
lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Draw up an inventory of electrical equipment and tools. 
-Inspect weekly. 
- Keep operating instructions available for staff
- Use double-insulated equipment
- Keep an up-to-date inventory of chains, hooks and other removable lifting accessories used for securing, lifting or transporting loads or personnel
- Keep a copy of inspection certificates issued by an approved body
- Remove from service any equipment or accessories that have suffered damage, even partial

lignesRisque.sourceDanger: - Defective equipment leading to an accident
lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Before signing for acceptance:
  ° Visually inspect the machine (presence of guardrails, attachment point, absence of deformation, etc.) 
  ° Check the validity of the inspection certificate from the approved inspection body (SECT)
  ° check and test the controls both at ground level and in the basket.

- Store each cylinder in an upright position
- Store oxidising gases (oxygen) separately from combustible gases (acetylene, propane, methane, etc.): whether the cylinders are empty or full
- Regularly remove empty cylinders
- Keep the storage area away from all activity
- Restrict access to a single authorised person

- Limit the height of stacked items
- Where necessary, use equipment that facilitates storage (racks, bins, etc.) for better stability and easier handling

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Locate the storage area at a sufficient distance from unstable ground (sand, etc.), trenches, excavations and embankments
- Ensure the ground bearing capacity is adequate; reinforce it (plates, etc.) if necessary

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Check that the list of hazardous products is included in the safety plan
- Regularly tidy the storage room (keep the different hazardous products separated, etc.)
- Check that each cylinder (full or empty) and/or container is properly closed, regularly check the tightness and the presence of the protective cap on the cylinders
- Comply with the storage and safety instructions recommended by the manufacturer

- Smoking prohibited
- Store hazardous products in a room away from any heat source (sun, etc.), preferably ventilated
- Store only the quantities needed to meet immediate requirements
- Post the appropriate signage at the entrance to the room (prohibitions and obligations): risks and measures to be taken
- Clearly identify each hazardous product and store them separately
- Place fire-fighting equipment (extinguishers, etc.) at the entrance to the room
- Restrict access to the storage room to authorised persons only (preferably a lockable room)
- Choose a room sheltered from the sun and with sufficient ventilation

probabilite.texte: Possible if multiple issues occur simultaneously

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention: -Keep hazardous products in their original packaging (in particular, do not mix different products that could cause a chemical reaction)
- Check the legibility of the labels on each container (precautions for use, instructions for use, etc.)
- Use storage racks for round materials

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Sort waste and dispose of it in the containers provided for this purpose: paper and cardboard, metals, packaging plastics, construction waste (bricks, concrete, etc.), flammable or toxic chemical products…
- Have the containers emptied regularly
- Place the containers away from work zones (see site layout plan)
- Put the net back over the container

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Keep waste away from any heat source
- Do not burn waste (paper, cardboard, plastics, etc.)

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Comply with the manufacturer's instructions for use, safety and disposal (packaging, etc.)
- Never dispose of into the sewer
- Contact the prevention advisor in case of doubt

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Use a trolley and secure the cylinders to it. Never roll cylinders along the ground
- Check the pressure of each cylinder
- Fit the protective cap on each cylinder to protect the valve
- Never lift or carry a cylinder by its cap or valve
- Do not overestimate your physical strength; ask one or more colleagues for help and use suitable handling equipment

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention: - Check that each container is sealed and properly closed

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention: - Smoking prohibited

- Ensure a firm grip and, if necessary, use handling straps, ropes, removable handles…
- Clear the walkways and have a colleague guide you
- Only handle the quantities needed to meet immediate requirements

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Check that lifting appliances and equipment have undergone their quarterly inspection by an accredited body (inspection certificate)
- Ensure the ground has sufficient bearing capacity
- Mark off the lifting zone and prevent access to it
- Never lift loads above people
- Properly secure the load to be lifted
- Follow the operating, maintenance and safety instructions
- Check for the absence of obstacles or power lines before raising the load
- Guide the load during lifting using a rope for particularly bulky elements

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.sourceDanger: General measures for all types of work at height
lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Clear the work area of all obstacles (at ground level and at height) and mark out a safety work zone to prevent other workers from passing nearby
- Check the strength, stability and slope of the ground and shore it up if necessary
- Check the strength and stability of the ladder, scaffolding, scissor lift…

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.sourceDanger: General measures for all types of work at height
lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Move the ladder, scaffolding, etc. as often as necessary, warning nearby workers beforehand
- Do not place a ladder or scaffolding in front of a door. If unavoidable, lock the door and place a warning sign on the other side to alert third parties. Keep the blocking time as short as possible
- Keep the ladder and scaffolding clean and in good condition (uprights, rungs, platforms…)
- Do not work at height if you suffer from vertigo

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.sourceDanger: General measures for all types of work at height
lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention: - Use ladders or elevating equipment well away from electrical cables

- Install guardrails on staircases and inspect them regularly
- Remove transport protection mats; replace with wooden boards if necessary; where removal/replacement is not possible, check and refasten them regularly

- Do not work above other workers
- Give preference to collective protective equipment (guardrails, stair scaffolding) over personal protective equipment (harnesses…)
- Favour the use of platforms or scaffolding to carry out work (rather than ladders)

probabilite.texte: Possible if multiple issues occur simultaneously

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- The MEWP must be moved by an authorized person
- Do not exceed the maximum load (number of people, materials or equipment…)
- Choose the type of elevating platform according to the local situation (indoors or outdoors), the available surface area (manoeuvring space) and the required height

probabilite.texte: Possible if multiple issues occur simultaneously

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Check that the guardrails are present and correctly fitted
- Keep the amount of materials or tools on the platform to a minimum to avoid overloading the lift, and distribute them correctly to prevent any imbalance
- Do not use the platform guardrails as a ladder or support
- Check that the equipment has a valid inspection certificate from an accredited body; carry out a visual inspection before each use

probabilite.texte: Possible if multiple issues occur simultaneously

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Identify and remove any defective ladder from use
- Never cut a ladder down to size
- Check the stiles: must be straight
- Check every rung: all present and straight
- Check that the anti-slip feet are present and in good condition
- Use the ladder for moving to height and for light, short-duration work only - for anything else: use scaffolding
- When used to change level: the ladder must extend at least 1m (3 rungs) above the landing point; secure the top of the ladder if it has more than 25 rungs or in bad weather (wind, etc.)
- Never use a ladder as a scaffold platform or as a walkway
- Place a board at the foot of the ladder when the ground is not sufficiently stable
- Never extend a ladder using improvised means. Always use a ladder of sufficient length
- Check that the ladder is kept at the correct angle (75 degrees)
- Do not lean out to reach a distant point; move the ladder as often as necessary instead
- Do not climb the ladder while carrying heavy or bulky objects

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention: - Move the ladder with several people if it is heavy

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention: - Use insulated ladders (wood, carbon fibre, polyester) where there is a risk of electrocution

- Erection to be carried out by, or under the supervision of, an authorized person
- Identify and set aside any defective scaffolding components
- Clear a sufficient work area for erecting, dismantling, moving and storing the scaffolding
- Handle each component with care (do not throw components onto the ground)
- Put the scaffolding away without delay after dismantling
- Affix the VMA sud scaftag
- Inspect the scaffolding before each use, once a week, and after any prolonged interruption of work
- Provide protective measures at the foot of the scaffolding to prevent collisions or to divert traffic
- Ensure that the maximum height of the scaffolding platform does not exceed three times the width of its smallest base, including the outriggers
- Do not position the platform more than 20 centimetres from the wall

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Lock the castors of the scaffolding
- Keep the amount of materials or tools on the scaffolding to a minimum to avoid overloading it, and distribute them correctly to prevent any imbalance
- Move carefully on the platform (do not jump)
- Regularly keep the platform clean and tidy (materials, tools…)
- Clean and maintain the scaffolding components before storing them
- Do not move the scaffolding unnecessarily
- Mark off the area where there is frequent passage or traffic

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Check that the drill bit is properly sharpened and correctly fitted
- Use water, where applicable, to cool the bit while drilling

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Take the necessary measures to prevent water damage; install protective tarpaulins if necessary
- Drill perpendicular to the work surface - Check for the absence of electrical cables or pipework at the drilling location

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention: - Warn workers near the work area; offer the use of PPE (hearing protection)

- Never point the laser at a reflective surface or at anyone
- Inform third parties that a laser is in use, of the risks involved and of the precautions to be taken
- Never leave the laser unattended
- Only switch the laser on when necessary and switch it off at other times

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Isolate the work area from other rooms to prevent dust from spreading to adjacent premises
- Close the ventilation vents
- Switch off the ventilation system
- Dampen the work area and the waste, where possible, when removing it
- Extract dust at source (chasing, drilling work…)

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Point the tool in a non-hazardous direction
- Hold the tool perpendicular to the work surface and never point it at anyone
- Check the thickness and consistency of the work surface
- Check that the cartridge power matches the nail/fastener being used
- The tool must only be used by a competent person with sufficient experience or specific training, who is over 18 years of age
- Inform third parties that the tool is in use, of the risks involved and of the precautions to be taken

probabilite.texte: Possible if multiple issues occur simultaneously

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Use clamping equipment suited to the workpiece and the type of work to be carried out (vice, locking pliers, clamps…)
- Hold the tool with both hands

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.risques: - Respiratory irritation, dust build-up in the lungs
lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Mark off the work area
- Warn third parties
- If necessary, for lengthy operations, dampen the work surface to limit dust generation

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention: - Advise third parties to move away for the duration of the work or to wear hearing protection
- Take the necessary measures to prevent damage caused by flying debris (protection of walls, tiling, windows…)

- Check that the disc/blade is correctly fitted and that the guard is in place
- Use supports or ask a colleague to help hold the workpiece being cut. Never hold the workpiece with your foot
- Use a disc that is in good condition and suited to the material being cut
- Check that no third parties are nearby

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- If necessary, request a hot work permit from the Client
- Remove all flammable materials from the area

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Use supports for the pipes
- Guard moving parts against anything that could jam the machine
- Mark off the work area

probabilite.texte: Possible if multiple issues occur simultaneously

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
-' Plan the operation in advance and communicate with stakeholders
- Demarcate the work zone and prevent access by unauthorised persons 
- Ensure the proper stability and fixing of the removed/dismantled elements

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.sourceDanger: Installation, stripping, connection and insulation testing of cables in the HV cabin, HV transformer, main LV switchboard, backup generator, UPS,
lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Demarcation of the work zone with signage preventing access
- Connections shall be carried out by a person qualified BA5
- Lockout/isolation of non-essential circuits
- Tests and checks before energising

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Prior verification and approval of feasibility with the client and/or safety coordinator
- Communication to stakeholders of the switching on/off
- Training and authorisation for switching on/off
- Demarcate, prevent and prohibit access to the work zone
- Lockout in the event of switching off (7 golden rules)

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Prior verification and approval of feasibility with the client and/or safety coordinator
- Communication to stakeholders of the switching on/off
- BA4 qualification or supervision by a BA5-qualified person
- Demarcate, prevent and prohibit access to the work zone
- Application of the seven golden rules of lockout
- Earthing of the generator

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.sourceDanger: Installation of cable tray/ladder supports at a height of less than 2 m using a stepladder and specific tools (angle grinder, drill, welding set, etc.)
lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Only use the stepladder if and only if it is not reasonably possible to use small mobile scaffold towers
- Check that the stepladder has a valid annual inspection (sticker/tag)
- Regularly check (at least once a day) the condition of the non-slip rubber feet of the stepladders 
- Only personnel authorised for work at height may use the stepladder
- Demarcate the work zone
- Use the wrist lanyards of portable tools

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.sourceDanger: Installation of cable tray/ladder supports at a height of less than 2 m using a stepladder and specific tools (angle grinder, drill, welding set, etc.)
lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention: - Protection of cables against any external damage and perfect insulation

lignesRisque.sourceDanger: Installation of cable tray/ladder supports at a height of less than 2 m using a stepladder and specific tools (angle grinder, drill, welding set, etc.)
lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Hot work permit
- Zone demarcated according to possible projections

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.sourceDanger: Installation of cable tray/ladder supports at a height of less than 2 m using a stepladder and specific tools (angle grinder, drill, welding set, etc.)
lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Solidly cover, properly close off or demarcate (min. distance 1.50 m) hazardous floor openings
- Install guardrails (compliant: top rail, mid-rail, toe board) or safety nets for vertical openings

lignesRisque.sourceDanger: Installation of cable tray/ladder supports at a height of more than 2 m using scaffolding or a mobile elevating work platform (MEWP), using specific tools (angle grinder, drill, welding set, etc.)
lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
Scaffolding:
- Use appropriate scaffolding, erected by competent workers under the direction of a competent and authorised person
- The scaffolding must be inspected daily, the scaftag must be replaced every week
- The brakes must be locked when a worker is on the scaffold.
- Top rails, mid-rails and toe boards must be present at all times
- The work zone must be demarcated
- No relocation may take place with a person or material present on the platform.
- Identify the route and obstacles before beginning to move
MEWP:
- MEWPs shall be inspected when unloaded from the truck (visually, valid periodic inspection)
- Only authorised personnel may move the MEWPs

lignesRisque.sourceDanger: Installation of cable tray/ladder supports at a height of more than 2 m using scaffolding or a mobile elevating work platform (MEWP), using specific tools (angle grinder, drill, welding set, etc.)
lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention: - Protection of cables against any external damage and perfect insulation

lignesRisque.sourceDanger: Installation of cable tray/ladder supports at a height of more than 2 m using scaffolding or a mobile elevating work platform (MEWP), using specific tools (angle grinder, drill, welding set, etc.)
lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Hot work permit
- Zone demarcated according to possible projections

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.sourceDanger: Cable pulling at a height of less than 2 m using stepladders and specific tools (jack-and-spindle or cable drum unwinder)
lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Only use the stepladder if and only if it is not reasonably possible to use small mobile scaffold towers
- Check that the stepladder has a valid annual inspection (sticker/tag)
- Regularly check (at least once a day) the condition of the non-slip rubber feet of the stepladders 
- Only personnel authorised for work at height may use the stepladder
- Demarcate the work zone
- Use the wrist lanyards of portable tools

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.sourceDanger: Cable pulling at a height of less than 2 m using stepladders and specific tools (jack-and-spindle or cable drum unwinder)
lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention: - Protection of cables against any external damage and perfect insulation

lignesRisque.sourceDanger: Cable pulling at a height of less than 2 m using stepladders and specific tools (jack-and-spindle or cable drum unwinder)
lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Hot work permit
- Zone demarcated according to possible projections

probabilite.texte: If everything goes wrong at once

lignesRisque.sourceDanger: Cable pulling at a height of less than 2 m using stepladders and specific tools (jack-and-spindle or cable drum unwinder)
lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Solidly cover, properly close off or demarcate (min. distance 1.50 m) hazardous floor openings
- Install guardrails (compliant: top rail, mid-rail, toe board) or safety nets for vertical openings

lignesRisque.sourceDanger: Cable pulling at a height of less than 2 m using stepladders and specific tools (jack-and-spindle or cable drum unwinder)
lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
- Stabilise and secure cable drums and unwinders
- Demarcate the unwinding zone as well as the route taken by the cable
- Check the cable retention systems (sleeves/couplings, etc.)

lignesRisque.sourceDanger: Cable pulling at a height of more than 2 m using scaffolding or a MEWP and specific tools (jack-and-spindle or cable drum unwinder)
lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:
Scaffolding:
- Use appropriate scaffolding, erected by competent workers under the direction of a competent and authorised person
- The scaffolding must be inspected daily, the scaftag must be replaced every week
- The brakes must be locked when a worker is on the scaffold.
- Top rails, mid-rails and toe boards must be present at all times
- The work zone must be demarcated
- No relocation may take place with a person or material present on the platform.
- Identify the route and obstacles before beginning to move
MEWP:
- MEWPs shall be inspected when unloaded from the truck (visually, valid periodic inspection)
- Only authorised personnel may move the MEWPs

lignesRisque.mesuresPrevention:

- In confined spaces, interventions are always carried out by at least 2 workers
